en.title: Since Jesus Came into My Heart
en.author: Rufus H. McDaniel
stanzas:
[A]What a wonderful change in my life has been wrought
Since [D]Jesus came into my [A]heart;
I have light in my soul for which long I have sought,
Since [B7]Jesus came into my [E7]heart.

I have ceased from my wand'ring and going astray,
Since Jesus came into my heart;
And my sins which were many are all washed away,
Since Jesus came into my heart.

I'm possessed of a hope that is steadfast and sure,
Since Jesus came into my heart;
And no dark clouds of doubt now my pathway obscure,
Since Jesus came into my heart.

There's a light in the valley of death now for me,
Since Jesus came into my heart;
And the gates of the City beyond I can see,
Since Jesus came into my heart.

I shall go there to dwell in that City I know,
Since Jesus came into my heart;
And I'm happy, so happy as onward I go,
Since Jesus came into my heart.
en.chorus:
Since [A]Jesus came into my heart,
Since [D]Jesus came into my [A]heart;
Floods of joy o'er my soul like the sea billows roll,
[D]Since [E7]Jesus came into my [A]heart.

notes: Text from Timeless Truths, which cites hymnary. Hymnary's representative text (Our Great Redeemer's Praise #552) has the same five stanzas; it reads 'I have light in my soul for which long I sought' (simple past) where TT has 'long I have sought', drops the article in the refrain's third line, lower-cases 'city', and ends the second line of several stanzas with an exclamation mark. TT kept; the score sings 'long I have sought'. Tune MCDANIEL (Charles H. Gabriel, 1914), meter 12.8.12.8 with refrain. Key: hymnary's instances run 22 A-flat to 18 A; TT prints A. A is a guitar key and nearly as common, so nothing was transposed. Chords derived from the Timeless Truths MusicXML score by reading the four-part chord on every beat. Stanza: I with IV/A and sus4 neighbours over the tonic pedal (dropped), a iii7 on the pickup 'Since' dropped, IV, I; second half the same with II7 (V of V) on 'Jesus' and a half cadence on V7. Refrain: I, IV-I, then IV on the last 'Since' into a cadential 6/4 written as the E7 it is. COPYRIGHT: 1914, public domain in the United States; McDaniel died 1940 and Gabriel 1932, so the words are clear under life-plus-70 terms from 2011.
